source: The Triple D framing — dream, default, disaster — as a fixed set of three assumption bundles applied to any life event, so every scenario is shown three ways rather than as one number.
confidenceNote: The three bundles are a convention chosen here: which return percentile, what income does after the event, how long the gap runs. None is a forecast; the point is the spread between them, not any one column.
note: returns names a percentile in data/return_bands.json; incomeAfter multiplies income once the event's gap has passed; gapMultiplier scales the template's own gap; shock names a one-time hit the engine knows how to price. BRIEF §6.1, D-086.
